Story: Create an account and log in
I want to: create an account and log in without reading a manual
So that: I can start setting up my study the same day
Acceptance criteria: The password rules appear before I type. | If a field is wrong, a summary at the top says which one and takes me to it. | Log in and Create account open in a dialog over the home page, and Esc closes it and returns the focus. | After logging in, I return to the page I had requested.

Story: Learn to use it on first access
I want to: be guided through the screens the first time and have help on each page
So that: I do not get stuck on a screen I do not understand
Acceptance criteria: On first access, a tour shows the actions on the real screens, and I move forward by doing the action. | I can skip or close the tour and review it later from the help. | Every researcher page has a (?) that explains that page.

Story: Create a study with two versions
I want to: register the study with the two versions of the app
So that: I can compare the current version with the new one in the same study
Acceptance criteria: I enter the title, product, objective, period and versions. | The product name suggests the name of the first version. | Errors appear in a summary with a link to each field, and nothing is lost. | The study starts as a draft, without accepting responses.

Story: State who is responsible for the research
I want to: state in the consent form who I am, how to contact me, the risks and the benefits
So that: I comply with research ethics and inspire trust in those who respond
Acceptance criteria: Name, contact email and institution are filled in from my account and are mandatory. | Risks and benefits come with a suggested text that I can change. | The ethics committee is optional and appears in the consent form when provided. | I see the preview of the participant's consent form next to the form.

Story: Decide whether to collect demographic data
I want to: choose, for each study, whether the link asks about age group, gender, education and familiarity
So that: I collect only what my research needs
Acceptance criteria: Demographic data collection is off by default. | When I turn it on, the consent form says so and the estimated time increases. | Demographic data is stored encrypted in the database.

Story: Open data collection and send the link
I want to: open data collection and copy the link with one click
So that: I can send it to the patients' WhatsApp group
Acceptance criteria: Open data collection confirms what changed in a message: "Data collection open. The link already accepts responses." | Copy link copies and announces that it copied, also from the keyboard. | The link is short, and the link of another study cannot be guessed.

Story: Follow the data collection
I want to: see how many people have already responded and when the last response arrived
So that: I know whether I need to promote the link more
Acceptance criteria: The study list shows the responses and the last response of each study. | The bell reports new responses, grouped while I have not read them.

Story: Understand the result without being a statistician
I want to: read the result with the written interpretation next to each number
So that: I know whether the new version is better without becoming an expert
Acceptance criteria: A sentence at the top summarizes the result. | Each scale shows the mean, CI95, alpha, interpretation and benchmark range, in the chart and in a table. | Technical terms have a short explanation that opens right there. | With low alpha or a small sample, a warning says what it means and what to do. | The chart remains readable without depending on color.
Requirements: RF38, RF43, RF44, RF45, RF49, RNF07, RNF08

Story: See which items pulled the scale
I want to: see the mean of each of the 26 items
So that: I can explain in my dissertation why a scale scored low
Acceptance criteria: The chart shows each item between its two terms. | I can view it in the official order or grouped by scale.

Story: Compare the two versions
I want to: see the versions side by side in the same chart
So that: I can say on which scales the new version did better
Acceptance criteria: Each participant goes to the version with the fewest responses, so the groups stay similar. | Each version has a marker of a different shape, and a sentence points out the largest differences. | The version and the mode are kept in the address: reloading or sending the link keeps the same view.

Story: Take the results to the dissertation
I want to: download the table per scale and the dashboard as PDF
So that: I can put them in the text without redoing charts
Acceptance criteria: The per-scale CSV opens in Excel in Portuguese, with a decimal comma. | The PDF has the study title, n and date in the header.

Story: Remove careless responses from the analysis
I want to: see which responses look careless and remove them from the calculation
So that: those who answered at random do not distort the result
Acceptance criteria: The tool flags as suspicious anyone with 3 or more inconsistent scales or more than 15 identical answers. | I see the reason and the range of each of the participant's scales. | I remove and return them one by one, or all the suspicious ones at once, without deleting anything. | The dashboard numbers then use only those in the analysis.

Story: See the profile of the respondents
I want to: see the distribution of the demographic answers
So that: I can describe the sample in my dissertation
Acceptance criteria: Each question appears in a chart with the table of numbers. | I can filter by version. | Prefer not to say and those who skipped appear separately.

Story: Close and reopen data collection
I want to: close data collection at the end of the period and reopen it if needed
So that: I stop receiving responses without losing the ones I already have
Acceptance criteria: Once closed, the link explains that data collection has ended. | Reopening makes it accept responses again.

Story: Correct the study after creating it
I want to: edit the data and the versions
So that: I can fix a typo or add a version
Acceptance criteria: The changes are saved and a message confirms it. | While data collection is open, I cannot remove a version that already has responses.

Story: Delete a test study
I want to: erase the study I created for testing
So that: my list stays clean
Acceptance criteria: The dialog says how many responses go with it. | It is only deleted after I type the study title.

Story: Take care of my account data
I want to: change my details, download what the tool stores about me and delete the account
So that: I can exercise my LGPD rights without asking anyone
Acceptance criteria: I change my name and email in My account; an email belonging to another account is rejected. | Download my data delivers a JSON with the account, without the password. | Deleting the account asks for my email and also erases my studies. | The privacy policy explains what is stored and why.

Story: Check the numbers in the official spreadsheet
I want to: export the responses into the UEQ Data Analysis Tool itself
So that: I can check that the tool calculates like the spreadsheet before signing a paper
Acceptance criteria: The official spreadsheet comes out filled in with the 26 values of each participant in the analysis, starting at Data!A4, and recalculates when opened in Excel. | The recoding and the statistics follow the formulas of the handbook and the spreadsheet. | The questionnaire does not lead the answer: the 7 positions have the same visual weight. | The numbers match the spreadsheet with a tolerance of 1e-6.

Story: Merge responses collected on paper
I want to: import the responses from an event from a CSV
So that: I can analyze everything in the same dashboard
Acceptance criteria: I see a preview before importing. | Rows with errors are pointed out by number, and nothing is imported while there is an error. | The imported responses appear marked as imported.

Story: Follow my student's study
I want to: be invited to Marina's study as a viewer
So that: I can see the same dashboard as she does without being able to change anything
Acceptance criteria: The invitation arrives in the bell and I accept or decline it. | As a viewer, I view and export, but I do not edit or delete. | I only see the studies that are mine or that have been shared with me.

Story: Know what changed in the studies
I want to: be notified when the team changes a study or responses arrive
So that: I do not need to open each study to find out
Acceptance criteria: The bell shows invitations, new responses and changes made by partners. | The notifications are also sent by email, in my language, and I can turn them off in My account.

Story: Protect the account on a shared computer
I want to: change the password and know that the other sessions are ended
So that: I do not leave the account open in the lab
Acceptance criteria: Changing the password ends the sessions in other browsers. | Anyone who opens a researcher page without a session is sent to Log in. | After 5 wrong passwords, the email has to wait before trying again. | The tool only works over HTTPS, with the security headers.

Story: Export the responses for another analysis
I want to: download the raw and the recoded responses
So that: I can run analyses that the tool does not do
Acceptance criteria: The raw CSV has the values from 1 to 7, the version and the demographic data. | The recoded CSV has the values from -3 to +3 with the polarity corrected. | The files open directly in Excel in Portuguese.

Story: Know the rule behind each number
I want to: see how each statistic is calculated and classified
So that: I can explain the method to an examining committee
Acceptance criteria: Pragmatic quality is the mean of Perspicuity, Efficiency and Dependability; hedonic quality, of Stimulation and Novelty. | Each mean is classified into the 5 benchmark ranges, and a mean equal to a limit falls into the lower range. | The interpretation uses the neutral range from -0.8 to +0.8.

Story: Apply the short version at events
I want to: apply the UEQ-S, with 8 items
So that: I can collect data at events where people have little time
Acceptance criteria: I choose between UEQ and UEQ-S when creating the study. | The form explains what changes between the two before I choose, and the choice is locked at the first response. | The participant answers the 8 pairs of the UEQ-S, with the short version's time in the consent form. | The results show, in their own tab, the pragmatic, hedonic and overall quality, with the UEQ-S benchmark, and export the official UEQ-S spreadsheet filled in.

Story: Use the tool in Japanese
I want to: switch the tool language to Japanese
So that: I can work in the language I read best
Acceptance criteria: I choose the language when creating the account, in My account or in the bar selector. | The change takes effect immediately, without leaving the page. | Without an account, the bar selector also changes it and it is kept in the browser.

Story: Run the study in Japanese
I want to: write the study in Japanese and have the link open in Japanese
So that: I can apply the questionnaire to participants in Japan
Acceptance criteria: I choose the study language in the form; the default is the account language. | The link opens in the study language, and the participant can change it. | Title, product and objective appear translated for anyone who switches language.

Story: Understand the invitation before accepting
I want to: read in one minute what it is about and what will happen
So that: I can decide whether I want to take part
Acceptance criteria: The consent form states the objective, estimated time, risks, benefits, data retention and who is responsible for the research. | I only take part after entering my age and clicking I agree. | I do not want to take part leaves without saving anything. | I can print or save a copy of the consent form and open the privacy policy without losing the form.

Story: Answer quickly on a phone
I want to: answer on my phone, with enlarged text, without an account
So that: I can finish in a few minutes
Acceptance criteria: I open the link without logging in and see no way into the researcher area. | Each circle has a touch target of at least 44 × 44 px. | Nothing scrolls horizontally at 320 px or with 400% zoom. | A fixed footer shows how many of the 26 items I have answered.
Requirements: RF24, RF27, RF28, RNF02, RNF05, RNF06, RNF23

Story: Know what I forgot
I want to: be told about the blank items when I submit
So that: I can correct them without searching item by item
Acceptance criteria: A summary at the top says how many are missing, with a link to each. | Nothing is saved while an item is missing.

Story: Not lose what I selected
I want to: recover my answers if the page reloads
So that: I do not have to start over
Acceptance criteria: Reloading the page brings back what I had selected, with a notice. | Switching language midway does not erase what I selected either.

Story: Give up without leaving a trace
I want to: leave in the middle of the questionnaire
So that: I am not stuck with something I no longer want to do
Acceptance criteria: Leave without sending asks for confirmation in a dialog. | On leaving, nothing I selected is saved.

Story: Skip the questions about me
I want to: not answer the demographic questions
So that: I do not disclose what I do not want to
Acceptance criteria: Every question has Prefer not to say. | I can skip the whole step. | The tool does not ask for my name, email or anything that identifies me.

Story: Know that it is over
I want to: see that my answers were recorded
So that: I can close the page with peace of mind
Acceptance criteria: After submitting, I see the thank-you message. | If I open the link again in the same browser, I see that I have already responded.

Story: Answer with a screen reader
As: Tiago, participant using a screen reader
I want to: answer using only the keyboard and NVDA
So that: I can answer as accurately as sighted people
Acceptance criteria: Each item is announced with its number, its two terms and the position of each circle. | Tab moves from item to item and the arrow keys change the position, with the focus always visible. | The summary of missing items receives the focus and is announced. | No screen has a WCAG 2.2 AA violation reported by axe-core.

Story: Answer in Arabic
I want to: answer in my language, with the validated Arabic terms
So that: I can answer better than in Portuguese
Acceptance criteria: The link opens in the browser language when it is one of the 37 UEQ languages. | The page flips to right-to-left, with the scale in the official order. | The terms are those of the official pack, never machine translation. | If the translation has not been approved by the UEQ authors, a notice says so.

Story: Take part with parental authorization
I want to: take part in a school study with my parents' authorization
So that: I can take part like my classmates who are of age
Acceptance criteria: The consent form asks for my age before I agree. | If I am under 18, I only take part after confirming the authorization of my parent or guardian. | Without an age, nothing is saved.

Story: Run the tool locally
I want to: get the tool running on my machine in minutes
So that: I can adapt it to my lab
Acceptance criteria: The README has the step-by-step guide, from the clone to the home screen. | The code is open source, under the MIT license.

Story: Change a threshold and recalculate
I want to: change a suspicion threshold without hunting for numbers in the code
So that: I can follow my group's protocol
Acceptance criteria: The thresholds are in data/protocolo.json, with their source. | A command recalculates the suspicion flag of the participations already stored.

Story: Prove that the calculation did not break
I want to: run the calculation tests after changing the code
So that: I am sure the numbers are still right
Acceptance criteria: The calculation is in a module of pure functions, with no database or interface. | Lint, types and unit tests each run with one command. | The tests cover the edge cases: n = 0, n = 1, all identical.

Story: Administer the lab accounts
I want to: see the accounts and create an account for a new student
So that: I can look after the lab installation
Acceptance criteria: Only an administrator can open the Administration page. | The administrator does not see anyone's studies, only the number per account.

Story: Demonstrate the tool without real data
I want to: create demonstration studies with made-up responses
So that: I can present the tool in a class
Acceptance criteria: Each scenario generates responses consistent with its profile. | The demonstration studies are kept in my account.

Story: Check the protection and the translations
I want to: see whether encryption is on and how much of each language is translated
So that: I know whether the installation is ready for a real study
Acceptance criteria: Administration shows whether the encryption key and email sending are configured. | Administration › Languages shows how much of each language has already been translated.

Story: Read the documentation without an account
I want to: read the documentation inside the tool, without creating an account
So that: I understand the architecture before making changes
Acceptance criteria: The Documentation tab opens for anyone. | Links between documents lead to the right spot, and the files on the document card download without an account. | Each diagram opens in full screen, with zoom.
